item.title: As diseases loom, CDC's response to measles deaths stirs fears about agency's reliability
item.description: The worst U.S. measles outbreak in decades is growing and flu season is imminent. Experts are fretting about federal health data reliability after the CDC questioned two Pennsylvania measles deaths.
item.content:encoded:
The worst U.S. measles outbreak in decades is growing and flu season is imminent. Experts are fretting about federal health data reliability after the CDC questioned two Pennsylvania measles deaths.

(Image credit: hapabapa/Getty Images)

item.title: 'I've never seen anything like this' -- A U.S. doctor treats Ebola's youngest victims
item.description: Dr. Rupa Narra is a U.S. pediatrician who arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo to help care for stricken children. Nothing could have prepared her for what she'd face.

item.title: Special education head at Education Department abruptly resigns

item.title: Whatever happened to the measles outbreak that shocked a country this year?

item.description: Arguing with a partner or a loved one can be anxiety-inducing. Conflict resolution facilitator Priya Parker explains how to start and end a fight — while easing dread for everyone.

item.title: Whatever happened to the Taliban threat: 'We will flog the women'?
item.description: In 2024, the ruling Taliban pledged to use flogging as well as stoning to punish people for not following certain of their precepts — committing adultery, running secret schools for girls. Have they followed through?
